Rosa, it is Paulo again. Two quick things before Thursday. First, I read your status update this morning and it was clear, so thank you. The only thing I changed was the last paragraph, because you wrote that the client confirmed the contract last week, and in fact they have not confirmed anything yet. They asked for a new proposal. That is a different sentence. Second thing: the figures for the third quarter came out yesterday and they are better than we expected. Your region is up nine per cent. I have already sent the file to your inbox. Have a look before the call, because somebody will bring it up.

Good morning. This is the weekly summary for the commercial team, and I will keep it to three points. Point one, the third quarter closed on Tuesday. We ended the quarter nine per cent above target in Brazil and four per cent below in Chile, and those are the final figures. Point two, what is still open. We have not signed the two contracts we discussed in August, and the client has asked for a new proposal in both cases. Point three, the deadline. Every account manager has to send the draft of the fourth quarter plan by the end of next week. Two of you have already sent it. Thank you, and please postpone anything else before you postpone that.

Paulo says he read the status update this morning and that it was clear. He explains that he changed the last paragraph because the client has not confirmed anything yet. Rosa says she wrote it after a phone call on Monday and that she will correct it. Paulo tells her the third quarter figures came out yesterday and that her region is up nine per cent. Rosa asks whether she should bring the figures up on the regional call, and Paulo says somebody certainly will.
